title: It's Her Party, I Can Hide If I Want To

beats.story: The second Caitlin slinks out with Garret at five p.m., Rhonda marches into my cubicle guns blazing -- and by guns, I mean the two giant Party City bags hanging from her arms. "You're my only decorator tonight," she announces, all business. "Garret's busy delaying Caitlin, and Marla's out sick with the stomach flu. Who gets the stomach flu this time of year? It's just a hangover or laziness." Damn it, the stomach flu was going to be my excuse to leave the party early tonight. Rhonda actually grabs the back of my chair and pulls it out so I'm forced to stand up. "We have so much to do. I've told Garret to give us one hour.
beats.story_cn: 凯特琳刚挽着加雷特在下午五点溜出去，朗达就炮火般冲进我的隔间——所谓炮火，指的是她臂弯里挂着的两个派对之城巨型购物袋。“今晚你是我唯一的装饰师，”她公事公办地宣布，“加雷特正拖住凯特琳，玛拉得了肠胃流感请病假。这节骨眼上谁会得肠胃流感？八成是宿醉或是犯懒。”见鬼，肠胃流感本该是我今晚提早离场的借口。朗达竟直接抓住我椅背把我拽起来，迫使我站定。“我们有一堆事要做。我让加雷特给我们一小时。”

beats.story: I got these spirals at Party Plus during lunch to put up in the bar." Part of me wonders what Rhonda would do if I just turned around and ran for the hills now, without any explanation. But her bright gaze, the lilt in her voice . . . her desolate Silver Timings profile she checks as often as she calls her son. She lives for this. And it's not like I can judge her for not having other things to do. Her frosty peach lipstick that has surely been discontinued is different from her normal shade.
beats.story_cn: “我午餐时在派对补给店买的这些螺旋彩带，正好挂酒吧里。”我暗自盘算，如果现在掉头就跑会怎样——不给任何解释。但她明亮的目光、上扬的语调……还有她那个和查看儿子消息一样频繁的“银色年华”相亲网站档案里荒凉的个人资料。她为这个而活。况且我又有什么资格评判她没有其他消遣？她那款肯定已停产的蜜桃色唇膏，颜色与平时不同。

beats.story: She's paired her nylon tights with heeled sandals, and her big toenail looks on the verge of cutting itself free. She dressed up for tonight . . . But it's not only that. I think of her smile when I was presenting in the multi-unit meeting. Her shy thank-you when I taught her how to use the online archive. I've always suspected that Rhonda was part evil, but maybe that part isn't as big as I thought.
beats.story_cn: 她用尼龙连裤袜搭配高跟凉鞋，大脚趾指甲看起来快要自己脱落。她为今晚特意打扮了……但不止如此。我想起多部门会议上我做汇报时她的微笑，教她使用在线档案系统时她羞涩的道谢。我一直怀疑朗达骨子里有部分邪恶，但或许那部分没我想的那么大。

beats.story: I take one of her bags and say, "Just let me know what you'd like me to do." The way she grins makes it feel like an act of mercy. I can be the bigger person here. And it may be best to give Caitlin a nice send-off, after all. The bar sits down the street from our building. As it's located in a corporate section of downtown, it's mostly frequented for office functions like ours. I've never been inside, but perhaps this is another thing I should start getting used to. If I'm going to be the new document lead in a few weeks' time, I may have to socialize with my team more. We climb down the creaky wooden staircase into the dimly lit basement room that boasts hardwood floor and walls and a lot of brass items throughout.
beats.story_cn: 我拎起她一个包，开口道：“您尽管吩咐。”她那咧嘴一笑，倒像我发了什么善心。罢了，就当成人之美。给凯特琳搞个体面欢送会或许也是应该的。酒吧就在我们写字楼这条街上，地处金融区，平日里多半是像我们这号人的办公聚餐才去。我从没进去过，但大概也该开始习惯这类场合了。毕竟几周后就要升任文档组主管，免不了要和团队多应酬应酬。我们沿着嘎吱作响的木楼梯往下走，走进那间灯光昏暗的地下室。硬木地板，木板墙，满屋子晃眼的黄铜装饰。

beats.story: The stale liquor scent roils my tummy. I try to imagine being a regular here -- one of the few who go for Friday drinks. Except the place has got all the workings of a bad time. The lighting is too bright to hide from, and there are too many standing tables so people can stare at you from all angles. Still, maybe with enough practice, it wouldn't be bad either. It could even be fun. Rhonda finds our reserved area in the back. She somehow produces a third giant bag that reads Dollars Plus and crinkles with every step as she marches to plop it on a corner table.
beats.story_cn: 酒精的陈腐气味熏得我胃里翻腾。我试着想象自己是这儿的常客——那些周五固定来喝一杯的人中的一个。可这地方分明就是场糟糕聚会的标配：灯光亮得无处躲，立桌摆得太密，让人从哪个角度都能被盯着瞧。不过，或许练着练着也就习惯了。甚至说不定还挺有意思。朗达在后头找到了我们预订的区域。不知怎么她又变出个第三个巨大的购物袋，上面印着"Dollar Plus"，一路窸窸窣窣作响，最后被她啪地甩在角落那张桌子上。

beats.story: Purple streamers spill out the sides; this decor is going to be so ugly and pointless. But the fact that she went to three different party shops crushes me. "Right." She claps her hands together. "How are you at standing on tables and making spirals with dual ribbon colors?" "I like to think I'm pretty great at that," I mutter. She actually squees. "Wait until you see the paper flowers I found!" I keep my smile plastered firmly on my face. It's like she's testing how far she can pull this shit without me getting angry enough to leave something not fully dead under her desk. We get to work tacking up weird paper shapes to the walls -- me mostly standing on the tables, and Rhonda handing me tape and telling me where to put it.
beats.story_cn: 紫色的彩带从两边垂下来——这装饰丑得毫无意义，简直令人发指。但想到她居然跑了三家派对用品店，我就泄了气。“好，”她拍了拍手，“你会站在桌子上用双色缎带做螺旋装饰吗？”“我在这方面，”我低声说，“自认颇有心得。”她居然兴奋得叫出声：“等你看到我找到的那些纸花！”我把假笑牢牢钉在脸上。这女人简直在试探我的底线，看我到底能忍到什么地步才会往她桌下塞点“不死也残”的东西。我们开始动手往墙上钉那些奇形怪状的纸制装饰——多半是我站在桌子上操作，朗达递胶带，指挥我往哪儿贴。

beats.story: I'm careful to follow her instructions as best I can. When we're done, she grabs my arm. "The fund has enough for everyone to get one drink, but if we order a few bottles of wine to share instead, we can have a drink now." She winks at me, all rebellious. "Actually, I might not stick around too long." Her mouth puckers so small that it cracks her lipstick. "What? The party hasn't even started. Have a drink with me; you've earned it." I stare toward the staircase. "I'm not sure .
beats.story_cn: 我谨遵她的指示尽力而为。结束后她拽住我的胳膊：“基金够每人点一杯酒，但如果我们点几瓶葡萄酒共享，现在就能喝上。”她朝我眨眨眼，带着叛逆劲儿，“其实，我可能不会待太久。”她嘴唇抿得极小，唇膏都裂开了。“什么？派对还没开始呢。陪我喝一杯，你该得的。”我望向楼梯，“我不确定……”

beats.story: . ." I start to say, but she's already at the bar. I'm not a social drinker anymore. People get in the way of real drinking. And socializing is the last thing a drunk person should be doing. Hasn't anyone else figured out this life truth? Before I can leave with my vibe intact, she returns, bottle in hand, and says, "Oh, come on, you're not going to leave me with this bottle of rosé alone?" She waves it in front of me, the pink liquid inside sloshing around and glinting against the bright lighting. Oh, if only Rhonda knew how familiar I am with this particular eight-dollar bottle.
beats.story_cn: ……“我刚要开口，她已走到吧台边。我不再是那个应酬喝酒的人了。人群妨碍真正意义上的痛饮。而醉鬼最不该做的事就是应酬。难道没人悟透这人生真谛吗？未等我保全气场转身离去，她已拿着酒瓶返回，说道：‘别这样，你不会让我独自对着这瓶桃红葡萄酒吧？’她在我眼前晃了晃酒瓶，瓶内粉色液体晃荡着，在明亮灯光下闪烁。哦，但愿朗达知道我与这瓶八美元廉价酒有多熟稔。”

beats.story: I glance at the time on my phone. Caitlin & Co. won't be here for a while yet. And I can't stand the idea of leaving Rhonda to sit here, drinking all by herself, mind wandering where it always goes when a lonely person is alone. So I resign myself to my fate and say, "Hit me." Once the wine is poured, she clinks our glasses together and says, "Cheers! You're not half as bad as I thought." I cough into my drink. Leave it to Rhonda to say exactly what she means. But I can respect it.
beats.story_cn: 我瞥了眼手机时间。凯特琳一行人还早着。而我无法忍受让朗达独自坐在此处喝酒，任思绪飘向独处者总会沦陷的深渊。于是认命叹道：“给我来一杯。”酒斟满后，她轻碰我的杯子说：“敬你！你没我想的那么糟嘛。”我呛得酒液直咳。这种大实话也只有朗达说得出口。但我欣赏这份直率。

beats.story: I give her a small smirk and whip back, "Neither are you." Her grin sharpens, her eyes wrinkling with mirth. And my chest lifts. She's not so bad. And, as it turns out, Rhonda can hold her own with a bottle. She quickly polishes off her first glass and pours us both a second, then makes quick work of that too. I'm idly listening to her tell a story about her latest knitting project when she suddenly pats me on the shoulder. I jolt, looking at her glossy plum nails against my plain black shirt. "I know you're not one to be overly friendly with people," she says, her eyelids drooping as she stares into her empty glass.
beats.story_cn: 我回以浅淡一笑，迅疾反击：“你也一样。”她的笑容变得锐利，眼中漾起愉悦的细纹。我的胸膛微微一松。她也没那么糟。而且，事实证明，朗达还能举杯对阵。她迅速喝完第一杯，给我们俩续上第二杯，转眼又干了个干净。我正心不在焉地听她讲最新编织项目的趣事，她突然拍了拍我的肩膀。我一激灵，目光落在她油亮的梅子色指甲上——那颜色衬着我朴素的黑衬衫。“我知道你不习惯对人过分热络，”她说着，眼帘低垂，凝视着空酒杯。

beats.story: "And that's fine. You like to keep to yourself. But I always wondered if you were mad at me for something." I shake my head. "Not at all!" And maybe that's true, if I can ignore all the times she's annoyed me, all the white-ink emails I've sent her through the years. Her gaze locks on to me, eyes soft and glassy. "I thought my Christmas decorations were nice." All the air deflates from my lungs. So I'm not the only one holding on to that little tiff from six years ago when I moved Rhonda's tinsel. I really am a miserable jerk.
beats.story_cn: “这没关系。你习惯保持距离。但我总在想，你是不是因为什么事在生我的气。”我摇摇头。“完全没有！”也许这是实话，如果我能忽略她所有惹恼我的时刻，忽略我这些年写给她的所有措辞严厉的邮件。她的目光锁住我，眼神柔和而朦胧。“我觉得我的圣诞装饰挺好看的。”我肺里所有的空气瞬间被抽空。原来，不止我一个人还记着六年前我挪动朗达的金属箔饰品引发的那场小争执。我果然是个可悲的混蛋。

Rhonda's face goes slack, like I've just relieved her of some momentous weight. "Thank you, dear. I shouldn't have held a grudge. I just love Christmas. But maybe you don't like religion in the office. It didn't used to be an issue, but I don't like to make people uncomfortable." I nod.
beats.story_cn: “是的，朗达，我真的很抱歉毁了你的装饰。那确实不好。我虽然不喜欢闪粉，但本可以处理得更好些。”朗达的表情松弛下来，仿佛我刚刚为她卸下了千钧重担。“谢谢你，亲爱的。我不该记恨的。我只是太爱圣诞节了。但或许你不喜欢办公室里有宗教气氛。这以前不是问题，但我不愿让人感到不适。”我点点头。

beats.story: "It wasn't that. I celebrate Christmas." Which, nowadays, is just an obligatory dinner at my parents' house, a small gift exchange, and a depress-y night in the apartment with whichever neighbor likes to blast Wheel of Fortune all evening. She brightens and grabs the wine bottle, pouring us both another glass. "Does your mom do a big turkey?" "An amazing one! Which is interesting since she grew up in Iran and didn't do Christmas there, yet she mastered it." Rhonda pauses, her wineglass halfway to her lips. "You're Iranian?" I involuntarily brace myself; I'm usually more aware of when I "come out" as Persian, but the wine loosened me up. Being white presenting, talking about my background is like playing Russian roulette. Most people are normal about it, but I've encountered enough of the type who get twitchy and start talking about their one friend or masseuse or whatever.
beats.story_cn: “倒不是那样，我也过圣诞节。”不过如今所谓节日，无非是去父母家吃顿义务晚餐、交换个小礼物，然后和某个总爱整晚大音量播放《幸运轮盘》的邻居各自枯坐公寓，共度沉闷长夜。她眼神一亮抓过酒瓶，给我们又续上一杯。“令堂会准备大烤鸡吗？”“妙极了！有趣的是她从小在伊朗长大，原本不过圣诞，却把这节日过出了精髓。”朗达举杯动作忽地停住，酒杯悬在唇边。“你是伊朗裔？”我不自觉地绷紧身体——我向来清楚自己何时该“坦白”波斯血统，但酒精让防线松弛了。顶着一张白人面孔谈论族裔背景，简直像在玩轮盘赌。多数人反应平常，但我也见识过不少那种瞬间僵住、开始喋喋不休讲自己某位伊朗朋友或按摩师的怪人。

Even when he did something disappointing, I was always so proud, so full of joy, to be his mom. It was the best time of my life." She's speaking in past tense. I can't help but think of my own mom -- the messages she sent today asking how work was going and to tell me about the newest fucked-up show she found on Discovery Channel.
beats.story_cn: “但我控制不住啊，这是我的人生。”喉间涌起硬块。我又灌下一口酒强咽下去。她效仿着深深啜饮。目光落在我们之间见底的酒瓶，眼瞳蒙上雾气。“我知道我总提他，但他曾让我无比骄傲。即使他做过让我失望的事，作为他的母亲，我始终满怀骄傲与喜悦。那是我人生中最美好的时光。”她在用过去式诉说。我忽然想起自己的母亲——今天发来的那些信息，问工作顺不顺利，讲她新发现的某档猎奇节目有多荒唐。

beats.story: That string of unanswered texts isn't much better than Rhonda's call log. "For what it's worth," I begin, trying to keep the emotion out of my voice, "I can tell you're a great mom." Rhonda holds up her nearly empty glass wineglass toward me. "I didn't think you were all bad, but it's good to be right." I clang my glass with hers. "To being right." And right when she raises her drink to polish off the last of our bottle, Garret walks in, trailed by two other guys from the finance team, Anthony Clark and Paul Chauncy. I've never spoken to them before; finance men tend to move in a pack, and the medley of cologne and hair gel odors makes me dizzy. "The lovers will be here in ten minutes," Garret announces to the room. "She thinks we're going on a double date to meet my new boyfriend, Eduardo." Rhonda nudges me and calls out, "Well, the party's ruined because nobody will believe that lie. You couldn't get a guy with such a sexy name.
beats.story_cn: 那一连串未回复的短信比朗达的通话记录也好不到哪去。“说句公道话，”我开口道，尽力不让情绪渗入声音，“看得出你是个很棒的妈妈。”朗达朝我举起她那几乎空了的酒杯，“我早觉得你没那么糟，看来我果然有眼光。”我与她碰杯，“敬有眼光。”就在她举杯要饮尽瓶中最后一点酒时，加雷特走了进来，身后跟着财务部的另外两人，安东尼·克拉克和保罗·乔恩西。我从未与他们交谈过——财务部的人总爱成群结队，混杂的古龙水与发胶气味熏得我头晕。

beats.story: The best you could get is a Bruce. Isn't that right, Jolene?" I try to chuckle, but more of Caitlin's friends from the office are trickling down the stairs, and all their eyes are narrowing in on me with expressions ranging from curiosity to suspicion. "I'll get more wine!" Rhonda announces gleefully, stumbling out of her seat and toward the bar. Garret's gaze trails from the clearly inebriated Rhonda to me, eyeing me like I'm a criminal. And this is my cue to leave. I stand up, intending to make my way outside as subtly as possible, when -- "Surprise!" everyone yells at once, and I am forced against the back wall as everyone crowds forward to greet Caitlin as she appears at the top of the staircase. She clutches a hand -- the one with the diamond on it -- against her chest in fake awe. "Oh god, you guys shouldn't have!" The throng encroaches on her.
beats.story_cn: “你顶多能找个布鲁斯。是不是啊，乔琳？”我试图干笑几声，但凯特琳办公室的更多朋友正陆续走下楼梯，所有目光都锁定在我身上，神情从好奇到猜疑不等。“我去拿酒！”朗达欢快地宣布，踉跄着离席走向吧台。加雷特的目光从明显醉意的朗达移到我身上，像审视罪犯般盯着我。这正是我离场的信号。我站起身，打算尽可能不着痕迹地走到室外，然而——“惊喜！”众人齐声高喊，我被挤向后墙，所有人涌上前迎接出现在楼梯顶端的凯特琳。她用戴着钻戒的手捂住胸口，装出惊喜状。“天哪，你们真不该破费！”人群向她围拢过去。

beats.story: A glass of bubbly appears in her hand. "Kyle!" Garret calls, as a guy makes his way into the room behind Caitlin. From my place in the back, I can make out only the top of his gelled dark hair. So this is the Kyle of Caitlin's Instagram, of hand and torso modeling fame. He's shorter than I pictured. He has his back to me as he greets Garret, but I can already tell that he's nothing special. His jeans are the Very Bad type -- I'd almost categorize them as a red flag. Caitlin takes a big swig of her champagne and walks up to him for a hug.
beats.story_cn: 一杯气泡酒出现在她手中。“凯尔！”加雷特招呼道，一个男人跟在凯特琳身后走进房间。从后排望去，我只能看清他油头粉面的发顶。原来这就是凯特琳INS里那位靠手模与腹肌出名的凯尔。比想象中更矮。他背对我与加雷特寒暄，但我已能断定他平平无奇。他穿的牛仔裤堪称灾难级——简直可以归入危险信号那一栏。凯特琳灌了一大口香槟，上前与他拥抱。

beats.story: His arm wraps around Caitlin's shoulders and pulls her in tight against his chest, and he whispers something to her without actually moving his face toward her, in that controlling man way. Finally, he turns to take stock of the crowd around them, and I get a decent glance at his face. All the air rips from my lungs. I fall back against the wall like it will offer some sort of camo. But it's too late. He flinches when he registers my face too, his eyebrows shooting up into his hairline. I'm Bambi in headlights. My head is spinning, like I've had five bottles of wine instead of half of one.
beats.story_cn: 他手臂一抬便箍住凯特琳的肩头，将她拽进怀里紧贴胸口，嘴唇未动却对她低语——完全是那种掌控欲十足的男人做派。末了他转头审视周遭人群，我恰好瞥见他的脸。肺里的空气瞬间被抽空。我背抵墙壁滑落，仿佛墙面能提供某种掩护。但已经太迟了。他认出我时也猛地一怔，眉毛高高挑进发际线。我像傻狍子似地杵在那儿，脑袋嗡嗡作响，仿佛灌下的是五瓶葡萄酒而非半杯。

And Kyle is standing right there, in front of the threshold. "Jo-Jo," he calls out as I get close. Before he can say anything else, I bolt past him and flee the room.
